title: Getting started with the plyranges package
text: Bioconductor two classes, IRanges GRanges, standard data structures representing genomics data. Throughout document refer either classes Ranges operation can performed either class, otherwise explicitly mention function appropriate IRanges GRanges. Ranges objects can either represent sets integers IRanges (start, end width attributes) represent genomic intervals (additional attributes, sequence name, strand) GRanges. addition, types Ranges can store information intervals metadata columns (example GC content genomic interval). Ranges objects follow tidy data principle: row Ranges object corresponds interval, column represent variable interval, generally object represent single unit observation (like gene annotations). Consequently, Ranges objects provide powerful representation reasoning genomic data. vignette, learn Ranges objects via grouping, restriction summarisation can perform common data tasks.

title: Additional examples of plyranges
text: Ranges objects can either represent sets integers IRanges (start, end width attributes) represent genomic intervals (additional attributes, sequence name, strand) GRanges. addition, types Ranges can store information intervals metadata columns (example GC content genomic interval). Ranges objects follow tidy data principle: row Ranges object corresponds interval, column represent variable interval, generally object represent single unit observation (like gene annotations). can construct IRanges object data.frame start width using as_iranges() method. can also construct GRanges object similar manner. Note GRanges object requires least seqnames column present data.frame (necessarily strand column).
code: library(plyranges) df <- data.frame(start = 1:5, width = 5) as_iranges(df) ## IRanges object with 5 ranges and 0 metadata columns: ##           start       end     width ##       <integer> <integer> <integer> ##   [1]         1         5         5 ##   [2]         2         6         5 ##   [3]         3         7         5 ##   [4]         4         8         5 ##   [5]         5         9         5 # alternatively with end df <- data.frame(start = 1:5, end = 5:9) as_iranges(df) ## IRanges object with 5 ranges and 0 metadata columns: ##           start       end     width ##       <integer> <integer> <integer> ##   [1]         1         5         5 ##   [2]         2         6         5 ##   [3]         3         7         5 ##   [4]         4         8         5 ##   [5]         5         9         5 df <- data.frame(seqnames = c("chr1", "chr2", "chr2", "chr1", "chr2"),                  start = 1:5,                  width = 5) as_granges(df) ## GRanges object with 5 ranges and 0 metadata columns: ##       seqnames    ranges strand ##          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> ##   [1]     chr1       1-5      * ##   [2]     chr2       2-6      * ##   [3]     chr2       3-7      * ##   [4]     chr1       4-8      * ##   [5]     chr2       5-9      * ##   ------- ##   seqinfo: 2 sequences from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths # strand can be specified with `+`, `*` (mising) and `-` df$strand <- c("+", "+", "-", "-", "*") as_granges(df) ## GRanges object with 5 ranges and 0 metadata columns: ##       seqnames    ranges strand ##          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> ##   [1]     chr1       1-5      + ##   [2]     chr2       2-6      + ##   [3]     chr2       3-7      - ##   [4]     chr1       4-8      - ##   [5]     chr2       5-9      * ##   ------- ##   seqinfo: 2 sequences from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths
